points out that MS evidence suggests that Act IV was not composed in the sequence of the
received text, and that it is therefore highly unlikely that the opening lines of the fourth act
could have been copied on 11 September; but the date may still stand as a strong indication
that S. had decided by that date to add a fourth act. The evidence of the nbks suggests that Act
IV was drafted in four sections, corresponding to lines 1–179, 194–318 (in Nbk 11), 319–502
(the exchange between Earth and Moon, probably the earliest conception for the Act, with
various complex drafts in Nbk 10, Nbk 11 and Nbk 12), and 519–78 (in Nbk 12). Act IV was
presumably written out, for the most part, in November and December 1819, after the Shelleys
